The AI Framework Hub

Where intelligence meets judgement.

Choose the student learning journey or open the staff portal. This uses the same working page structure as the History Hub: gateway first, sidebar navigation, one active page at a time, close buttons and deep topic panels.

AI Framework Hub

AI Literacy for Every Learner

Open a year group, choose a topic, launch a mission, use embedded resources and record a RAG judgement.

Choose your AI pathway

Each route opens separately and contains topic panels, embedded links, student tools and teacher pack connections.

AI Missions

Immersive challenge routes with objective, steps and success criteria.

FS2-Year 2

Play, notice, explain and stay safe.

Year 3-Year 6

Train, test and improve a model or rule.

Year 7-Year 9

Audit evidence, bias, provenance and impact.

Year 10-Year 13

Assure systems, defend decisions and govern responsibly.

Teacher Portal

Full topic-linked teaching packs with resources, QA evidence and Word-compatible download.

FS2 · Cause and effect

AI Conceptual Understanding

Teaching route

Hook image → retrieval → vocabulary → misconception → teacher think-aloud → guided role task → resource quest → independent judgement → RAG target.

Curriculum intent

Build AI literacy through explicit vocabulary, modelling, guided practice and visible student evidence.

Vocabulary

Input · output · data · model · prompt · evidence · source · bias · privacy · human oversight · safeguard.

Misconception

AI understands like a person.

Support and stretch

Support: sentence stems, vocabulary cards, paired talk, visual prompts. Stretch: compare two outputs, identify trade-offs and defend the stronger decision.

QA evidence

Collect student artefacts showing claim, evidence, limitation, safeguard and RAG next step.

Teacher resources

🔗 Lesson PPT deck🔗 AI4K12 Five Big Ideas🔗 AI4K12 resource directory🔗 Code.org · How AI Works🔗 Google AI literacy

Curriculum intent

Build AI literacy through explicit vocabulary, modelling, guided practice and visible student evidence.

Vocabulary

Input · output · data · model · prompt · evidence · source · bias · privacy · human oversight · safeguard.

Misconception

Working once means the solution is safe.

Support and stretch

Support: sentence stems, vocabulary cards, paired talk, visual prompts. Stretch: compare two outputs, identify trade-offs and defend the stronger decision.

QA evidence

Collect student artefacts showing claim, evidence, limitation, safeguard and RAG next step.

Foundation Stage · Ages 4-5 · AI Buddy: Dot · Discovery Bot

FS2 AI Literacy

Natural or machine helper. Sensors, sorting and safe adult help.

AI Conceptual Understanding
FS2AI Conceptual Understanding

Cause and effect

Explain the idea behind the system, data, model, training and output.

Resource links

🔗 Lesson PPT deck🔗 AI4K12 Five Big Ideas🔗 AI4K12 resource directory🔗 Code.org · How AI Works🔗 Google AI literacy

Immersive activity

Pupils use the visual hook to identify the AI system, the people affected, the evidence required, the benefit, the limitation and the safeguard. They work as designer, user, evidence checker and safety lead.

  • Bronze: identify what the system does.
  • Silver: explain what data, rule, model or prompt may affect the output.
  • Gold: judge one benefit, one risk and one improvement.
  • Platinum: defend a decision using evidence and a safeguard.

Big idea

Explain the idea behind the system, data, model, training and output. In this topic, pupils connect the concept to sensors, sorting and safe adult help using evidence rather than guesswork.

Teacher model

Think aloud: define the problem, name the data or evidence, test the response, identify one risk, then improve the prompt, rule, design or safeguard.

Common misconception

AI understands like a person.

Lesson sequence

  1. Retrieval: three key words and one likely misconception.
  2. Visual hook: inspect the image and identify input, output, data, people, benefit and risk.
  3. Teacher model: claim → evidence → limitation → safeguard.
  4. Guided pair task: designer, user, evidence checker, safety lead.
  5. Independent judgement: answer, improve, RAG next step.

Assessment evidence

Prompt log, model card, audit note, evidence table, risk card, policy statement, annotated output or design improvement.

Topic resources

Critical Evaluation & Informed Interaction
Year 8Critical Evaluation & Informed Interaction

Source, bias and provenance

Check evidence, question reliability, compare sources and improve prompts.

Resource links

🔗 Lesson PPT deck🔗 Common Sense AI literacy🔗 Khan Academy AI for Education🔗 UNESCO AI competency framework🔗 AI Literacy Day resources

Immersive activity

Pupils use the visual hook to identify the AI system, the people affected, the evidence required, the benefit, the limitation and the safeguard. They work as designer, user, evidence checker and safety lead.

  • Bronze: identify what the system does.
  • Silver: explain what data, rule, model or prompt may affect the output.
  • Gold: judge one benefit, one risk and one improvement.
  • Platinum: defend a decision using evidence and a safeguard.

Big idea

Check evidence, question reliability, compare sources and improve prompts. In this topic, pupils connect the concept to decision logic, provenance and data protection using evidence rather than guesswork.

Teacher model

Think aloud: define the problem, name the data or evidence, test the response, identify one risk, then improve the prompt, rule, design or safeguard.

Common misconception

A confident output is automatically reliable.

Lesson sequence

  1. Retrieval: three key words and one likely misconception.
  2. Visual hook: inspect the image and identify input, output, data, people, benefit and risk.
  3. Teacher model: claim → evidence → limitation → safeguard.
  4. Guided pair task: designer, user, evidence checker, safety lead.
  5. Independent judgement: answer, improve, RAG next step.

Assessment evidence

Prompt log, model card, audit note, evidence table, risk card, policy statement, annotated output or design improvement.
